tasks.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)

prep.what: Build the PostgreSQL-backed job queue with lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware dispatch, priority lanes, and a concurrency cap — the backbone the sweeper, CI runner, and deploy pipeline all sit on.
prep.understand: A lease-based queue uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` in Postgres to atomically claim a job row without blocking other workers. Workers hold a `lease_token` and must renew via heartbeat; if a heartbeat goes silent, a reclaim loop re-queues the job. Window-awareness means the queue checks that enough wall-clock time remains in the work window before dispatching a long job — so a 2-hour job never starts at 5:50 PM.
approach: Design the `jobs` table: `id, type, payload jsonb, priority int, status (queued/running/done/failed), lease_token uuid, leased_at, heartbeat_at, reclaim_after_s int, window_aware boolean, created_at, started_at, done_at, fail_reason text`.
Build `lib/job-queue.ts` with `enqueue()`, `claim()` (atomic `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), `heartbeat()`, `complete()`, `fail()`, and `reclaim()` (sweeps expired leases back to `queued`).
Add the window-aware gate: read `work_window.end` from `config.json`; if `end - now < job_estimated_duration`, skip dispatch and log the reason.
Write tests covering all axes: enqueue/claim race with two concurrent workers, heartbeat renewal, reclaim-after-expiry, priority ordering, window gate blocking a long job late in the day.
resources: Postgres `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` docs
`config.json` (work_window.start/end fields)
`lib/repository.ts` (existing DB patterns to follow)
Bun 1.3.14 on VPS (already installed, use as runtime reference)

tasks.title: Sweeper (per-repo sandbox, quality gate incl render+screenshot)

prep.what: Build the sweeper: the per-repo sandbox executor that pulls a job from the queue (t20), checks out the repo, applies the diff, runs the full quality gate chain in Docker, and returns a pass/fail verdict with gate details.
prep.understand: The sweeper wraps each repo in a Docker sandbox using the `RepoMapping` config established in t28. Inside, it runs `prepareCommands` (install/build) then the quality gates in sequence — one failure stops the chain. Critical: the daemon-side cross-process refresh lock (t29) must land before pointing the sweeper at live `SWEEPER_REPOS`; for now build and test against safe test repos only. The `refreshAndCheckBase` pattern from t28 handles freshness — call it before any gate runs.
approach: Build `lib/sweeper.ts`: claim a job from the queue (`job-queue.ts` from t20), run `refreshAndCheckBase()` (from t28), apply the diff to a temp worktree.

Implement the gate chain as named sequential steps: `compile` (tsc/build), `test` (test runner), `lint`, `build` (output artifacts), `render` (headless browser, assert no crash), `no-new-console` (grep for unexpected `console.error/warn` in output), `write-test` (assert a test file appears in the diff).
On any gate failure: call `queue.fail(jobId, { gate, output: lastNLines })` and stop — no further gates run.
On full pass: call `queue.complete(jobId, { artifact })`. Gate results and truncated output go into the job payload for the decision inbox.
resources: `docs/advisor-logs/2026-07-19-freshness-hardening.md` (refreshAndCheckBase, RepoMapping shape)

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Caught live on Harborview demo: rooms show 'unnamed' because PDFTron outlines ALL text (55 live words, zero room labels). v2 = (a) M3 tiles lane as opt-in AI action; (b) callout-vs-room filtering for Holabird noise.

prep.what: Productize the M3 vision tiles lane as an opt-in 'read labels (AI)' POST action, and add callout-vs-room filtering to eliminate UP arrows, FEC callouts, and general-note paragraphs from the label matcher.
prep.understand: Two root problems: (a) PDFTron-outlined-text firms have zero live-text bytes — the free lane returns nothing; the M3 tiles lane rasterizes the page into crops and sends them to MiniMax Vision (~4.3 min/sheet, costs metered credits via §7a). (b) Even on working sheets like Holabird the lane matches noise: stair arrows, FEC callouts, multi-line notes paragraphs. Key gate before going live: `MINIMAX_AI` key must be in the VPS `.env`.
approach: Wrap `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` into `engine/labels_m3.py`: tile the rendered page at 1024×1024 crops, batch-call MiniMax Vision (image attachments in the messages array), merge results by assigning each detected label to the room polygon whose centroid is closest.
Add `POST /sheets/{id}/read-labels` with a `mode` param (`free` = existing live-text lane, `ai` = M3 tiles lane); stream SSE progress events during tile processing so the UI shows progress.

Build the callout filter in `engine/labels.py`: reject multi-line blobs (split on newline, lines > 1), exclude short symbol strings near stair/elevator shapes by area-gate, add a min-polygon-area threshold so tiny annotation callouts don’t qualify as room names.
Verify on Harborview (target: 0 named → labeled rooms) and confirm Holabird stays ≥92/109 named (regression check).
resources: `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` (the existing working spike to productize)
MiniMax Vision API: `api.minimax.io/v1/chat/completions` with `image_url` content in messages
`MINIMAX_AI` key — must be added to VPS `.env` at `/opt/takeoff-engine/.env`

tasks.title: Door recall round 2 + bi-fold / cased-opening recall
tasks.notes: Door recall is THE constraint blocking global seal relax. Symbol-based detectors failed on furniture noise. UNBLOCKED by t15: localseal guard makes added chords SAFE. Raise recall via raster-gap detection.

prep.what: Push door chord recall higher using raster-gap detection on the binarized wall mask, targeting the 4 sheets still at 0.00 chord/GT-room coverage (holabird, mitchell, washington, merrimack).
prep.understand: Door recall is THE blocker on retiring the global `SEAL_FT`. The `localseal_guard` from t15 makes new chords SAFE — any bad chord that would merge two rooms self-reverts, so you can be aggressive on recall. Current chord coverage: 0.00 on 4/12 sheets, 0.32 on dental, 0.64 on brook_p4. At ≥0.6 average the global SEAL_FT retirement pays off per `w13_localseal_guard.py` measurements.
approach: Write `engine/doors_raster.py`: binarize the rendered wall layer at sealfill resolution, find thin white-gap regions (width < `door_max_ft × px_per_ft`, height > `door_min_h × px_per_ft`), propose each as a chord candidate.
Score candidates by confidence: gap aligned with a nearby wall-segment endpoint = high; isolated gap = low. Threshold at 0.5 and emit chord list.
Chain into the existing door detection pipeline in `engine/sealfill.py` after bi-fold detection — bi-fold runs first, raster-gap fills what symbol detection misses.
Re-run `docs/spike/w13_localseal_guard.py` on the updated chord set. Target: average coverage ≥0.6 across the 12-sheet corpus to unlock global SEAL_FT retirement.

tasks.title: Viewport-detection polish: KD-tree perf swap + frame-detect connectivity graft
tasks.notes: The one TODO left in tracked source (STATE.md:472, R13 era). Pure perf/robustness, zero GT movement expected.

prep.what: Two small R13-deferred polish items in `engine/viewport.py`: swap `KDTree` for `cKDTree` (C-accelerated, same API, meaningfully faster), and add a connectivity graft that verifies detected frame segments form a closed perimeter.
prep.understand: `cKDTree` is the compiled variant of `scipy.spatial.KDTree` — drop-in replacement, same call sites, O(n log n) neighbor lookups instead of pure-Python. The frame connectivity graft is a brief graph traversal after segment detection; log a `logger.warning` (never raise) when segments don't close. Both are zero-GT-movement changes — run the gauntlet to confirm.
approach: In `engine/viewport.py`, replace `from scipy.spatial import KDTree` with `from scipy.spatial import cKDTree as KDTree` — same call sites, no other changes needed.

After the frame-segment detection step, build a segment adjacency graph and check that all segments form a single connected perimeter (each endpoint within `gap_threshold` of another segment's endpoint); log `logger.warning` if not closed.
Run `python -m engine.gt.harness` — confirm all gauntlet checks pass with identical output, bit-for-bit.
Mark `STATE.md:472` TODO as closed: replace the comment with a completion note.
resources: `engine/viewport.py` (the file to edit — find `KDTree` import and the frame-detect step)
`STATE.md:472` (the tracked TODO to close)
